justification: Ports the frontend's proven battleaxe (flag-lot) detection to the Python lot-dimensions helper and feeds a battleaxe-aware width into the Housing-SEPP eligibility engine (upzoning tool + intelligence brief). Before: the Python helper returned no width for flag lots (the OBB model rejects shapes filling <60% of their box), so every width-gated form rendered 'unconfirmed' — a 4,189 m2 R3 lot (38 Park Rd Bowral) showed seven non-answers while Verify's frontend correctly measured a 16.31 m handle and 70.09 m developable head. The port keeps the TS thresholds verbatim and reproduces the frontend's verified output exactly on the real Bowral cadastre fixture (16.31/43.1/70.09/3710). Live end-to-end now shows Bowral: granny flat ELIGIBLE, dual occupancy ELIGIBLE, LMR forms correctly not-in-area.

pre_impl.existing_data: The proven algorithm already existed in the frontend (lib/geometry/lot-shape-analysis.ts detectBattleaxeLot + effective-lot-width.ts battleaxeAwareLotWidth, both test-backed) and produced the verified 16.31 m / 70.09 m Bowral result in Verify; the Python side already had the OBB frontage model whose <60%-fill rejection is exactly the flag-lot class. This PR ports rather than invents: thresholds, slice count and confidence scoring are kept verbatim from the TS source.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The prior assumption was that a null frontage on irregular lots was an acceptable conservative gap; the Verify screenshot comparison showed the same company already measures these lots correctly on another surface, so the gap was a siloed-capability defect, not a data limitation. Also corrected in passing: lot_dimensions imported LotDimensions via intelligence_brief although its true home is constraint_models (indirection removed, no cycle).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: the ported detector functions and the eligibility_lot_width helper in services/lot_dimensions.py, plus five optional backward-compatible fields on the LotDimensions pydantic model. Changed consumers: upzoning _lot_dims and the brief's eligibility width now use the battleaxe-aware helper. Deliberately NOT changed: constraint_arithmetic's frontage/depth estimation (setback geometry semantics differ from width-eligibility semantics — noted for follow-up), and the frontend TS implementation stays untouched as the reference.

functions.name: _detect_battleaxe
functions.input: Polygon points in real metres (closing point removed), from the Portal cadastre ring
functions.output: Dict with access-way width/length, main-lot width/area and confidence, or None when the lot is not a battleaxe
functions.if_none: None simply means not-a-battleaxe — calculate_lot_dimensions then classifies rectangular or irregular and the width falls back to the OBB frontage or stays None (engine unconfirmed path unchanged)

functions.name: eligibility_lot_width
functions.output: The developable head width for a battleaxe lot, otherwise the cadastral frontage; None when nothing usable exists
functions.if_none: Callers pass None straight into evaluate_eligibility, which marks width-gated forms unconfirmed and conservatively ineligible — identical to today's behaviour, so the change can only ADD resolved answers, never remove the conservative path

functions.name: _lot_dims
functions.input: Planning Portal property id integer, or None
functions.output: Tuple of lot area, battleaxe-aware eligibility width, and lot_type string for UI labelling
functions.if_none: Any gap returns (None, None, None); the page renders width as not-mapped and the engine keeps its unconfirmed handling

values.if_missing: Falsy or absent means fallback to frontage_m — a detector miss degrades to the previous behaviour, never to a fabricated width

values.read_at: frontend page header chip (Width (main lot, battleaxe) vs Frontage label)
values.if_missing: Null renders the plain Frontage label — labelling degrades, values do not

values.value: lot_dims_for_ca in the brief eligibility block
values.if_missing: eligibility_lot_width(None) returns None and the brief's eligibility falls back to the unconfirmed path exactly as before

queries: N/A - no SQL. Pure geometry on the already-fetched Portal cadastre ring; one real fixture file recorded from the live Portal for tests.

break_it.scenario: The port drifts from the TS reference (different slice count, thresholds or handle/head attribution) and silently reports a different width than Verify shows for the same lot
break_it.what_happens: Two surfaces of the same product disagree on a measurable number — the credibility failure this PR exists to close
break_it.how: thresholds kept verbatim and the golden test pins the Python output to the frontend's verified Bowral values to two decimals (16.31 handle, 70.09 head, 43.1 length, 3710 head area)

break_it.scenario: A rectangular or mildly irregular lot is misclassified as battleaxe and its width silently inflated to the max cross-section
break_it.what_happens: Width-gated forms could pass on a lot narrower than the minimum — a false eligible
break_it.how: detection requires ALL of: 6+ vertices, a sustained (3+ consecutive) narrow run under 40% of head width, head at least 9 m, strong min/max contrast and the narrow run a minority of length — the verbatim TS criteria; the rectangular test pins non-detection and frontage fallback

break_it.scenario: Detector crashes on a degenerate ring (duplicate points, zero-extent bbox) and takes the whole dimensions call down
break_it.what_happens: Lots that previously got area/frontage would start returning nothing — a regression for every lot, not just battleaxes
break_it.how: the detector guards zero extents, <6 vertices and <2 slice intersections by returning None (not-a-battleaxe), and the existing degenerate-polygon tests in the file still pass unchanged (29/29 then 2831 full suite)

break_it.scenario: The head width leaks into displays as if it were street frontage
break_it.what_happens: A 70 m 'frontage' on a lot with a 16 m street opening misstates the cadastre to users
break_it.how: the endpoint returns lot_type alongside the width and the page renders 'Width (main lot, battleaxe)' for flag lots instead of 'Frontage'; the response comment documents the semantics

break_it.scenario: The brief consumer change alters eligibility on non-battleaxe lots
break_it.what_happens: A blanket behaviour shift in the paid-adjacent brief rather than a targeted fix
break_it.how: eligibility_lot_width returns frontage_m verbatim for every non-battleaxe lot_type (including None from older payloads), so only flag lots change; full pytest incl. the brief goldens passes
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_lot_dimensions.py::TestBattleaxeDetection::test_rectangular_lot_is_not_battleaxe_and_keeps_frontage plus the full suite run

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after Railway deploy, run 38 Park Rd Bowral on the live tool: expect 'Width (main lot, battleaxe): 70 m', granny flat and dual occupancy green, LMR forms not-in-area. Kogarah spot-check unchanged.
